# AML Canada

> AML and regulatory compliance services in Canada. AML Canada helps money services businesses, virtual currency dealers, payment service providers and fintechs register with FINTRAC and the Bank of Canada (RPAA), build compliance programs under the PCMLTFA, run their compliance function with an outsourced compliance officer, prepare for examinations and train their staff. Operated by ComplyFactor Limited, a private consultancy not affiliated with FINTRAC or the Bank of Canada.

## Services

- [Outsourced compliance officer](https://amlcanada.ca/outsourced-compliance-officer.html): An outsourced Canadian AML compliance officer (MLRO): onboarding reviews, FINTRAC reporting, policies and risk assessments. US$1,500 per month for 10 hours.
- [MSB registration](https://amlcanada.ca/msb-registration.html): FINTRAC registration for money services businesses, foreign MSBs and virtual currency (crypto) dealers. Fixed fee US$3,500, prepared and submitted with you.
- [Compliance programs](https://amlcanada.ca/compliance-programs.html): PCMLTFA compliance program documents for FINTRAC-regulated businesses: policies and procedures, risk assessment, training and review plans. Fixed fee US$3,500.
- [Canadian business address](https://amlcanada.ca/canadian-address.html): A Canadian business address for foreign MSBs and companies entering Canada, for your setup, banking and partners. US$200 per month, terms agreed in writing.
- [MSB for sale](https://amlcanada.ca/msb-for-sale.html): Registered Canadian MSBs for sale now, from €28,000. Check each one on FINTRAC's registry before you pay. Due diligence and FINTRAC updates handled with you.
- [Buy or register an MSB](https://amlcanada.ca/buy-or-register-msb-canada.html): Two ways to a FINTRAC-registered MSB in Canada: buy a ready-made company from €28,000 or register your own for US$3,500. For founders in Canada and abroad.
- [RPAA registration](https://amlcanada.ca/rpaa-registration.html): Register as a payment service provider (PSP) with the Bank of Canada under the RPAA. Fixed fee US$3,500, plus the Bank's own application fee.
- [RPAA compliance program](https://amlcanada.ca/rpaa-compliance-program.html): RPAA frameworks for PSPs: governance, risk registers, incident response, third parties, safeguarding, cyber and continuity, annual reports. Fixed fee US$3,500.
- [Effectiveness reviews](https://amlcanada.ca/effectiveness-reviews.html): The FINTRAC two-year effectiveness review, often called an AML audit: your policies, risk assessment and training tested, with written findings.
- [Training](https://amlcanada.ca/training.html): Anti-money laundering training for MSB front-line staff, compliance teams and senior management, built to meet FINTRAC's training requirement.
- [Company incorporation](https://amlcanada.ca/incorporation-canada.html): Incorporate a Canadian company, federally or in Ontario, usually within 24 hours. Fixed fee US$1,500, ready for FINTRAC or RPAA registration.
- [Apostille & notarization](https://amlcanada.ca/apostille-notarization-canada.html): Apostille and notarization of Canadian corporate documents for foreign banks, payment partners and regulators, with a licensed Ontario partner notary.
- [Sell your MSB](https://amlcanada.ca/sell-your-msb.html): Sell a Canadian company registered with FINTRAC as an MSB. We check it, match it with a buyer, and handle the share sale and the FINTRAC updates.

## Guides

- [Ontario vs B.C. MSB registration: which province suits a crypto startup?](https://amlcanada.ca/ontario-vs-bc-msb-registration.html): Today there's no MSB difference between the two provinces. A money services business in Ontario or British Columbia registers with FINTRAC and nobody else, because B.C.'s Money Services Businesses Act has been passed but isn't in force. That should change: B.C. plans to start provincial registration, and Ontario has no equivalent law.
- [RPAA incident reporting and the 48-hour rule](https://amlcanada.ca/rpaa-incident-reporting.html): When a payment service provider becomes aware of an incident with a material impact, it must notify the Bank of Canada and the affected end users, payment service providers and clearing houses without delay. The Bank expects the first notice no later than 48 hours after the provider decides the incident is material.
- [RPAA vs FINTRAC MSB registration: do you need both?](https://amlcanada.ca/rpaa-vs-fintrac-msb-registration.html): Payment service providers register with the Bank of Canada under the RPAA. Money services businesses register with FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA. Many payment businesses are both, and the two registrations are linked: the Bank shares your application with FINTRAC and can refuse it based on what FINTRAC reports.
- [The RPAA annual report for payment service providers](https://amlcanada.ca/rpaa-annual-report.html): Every payment service provider that performs retail payment activities in a calendar year must file an annual report with the Bank of Canada by March 31 of the following year. It covers your risk management and incident response framework, safeguarding, activity metrics and financial results.
- [Who must register as a PSP under the RPAA?](https://amlcanada.ca/who-must-register-psp-rpaa.html): You must register with the Bank of Canada if you perform a payment function as a business in its own right, for electronic transfers in Canadian or foreign currency, with a link to Canada, and no exclusion applies. This guide shows how the Bank applies each part of that test to real business models.
- [Apostilling Canadian corporate documents for foreign banks and regulators](https://amlcanada.ca/apostille-corporate-documents-canada.html): Foreign banks, payment partners and regulators often want Canadian corporate documents with an apostille. Some government certificates can go straight to the authority. Most corporate records must be notarized first.
- [How to get an apostille in Canada (2026 guide)](https://amlcanada.ca/apostille-canada-guide.html): Since January 11, 2024, Canadian public documents going to Apostille Convention countries get an apostille. Who issues it depends on where the document was issued or notarized: Global Affairs Canada, or one of five provinces.
- [The travel rule and ministerial directives: what Canadian MSBs must do](https://amlcanada.ca/fintrac-travel-rule-ministerial-directives.html): Canada's travel rule requires money services businesses to send originator and beneficiary information with funds and virtual currency transfers, and to check it arrives with transfers they receive. Ministerial directives add stricter measures for transactions connected to Russia, Iran and North Korea.
- [FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties (AMPs) explained](https://amlcanada.ca/fintrac-penalties-amps.html): FINTRAC can impose administrative monetary penalties for breaches of the anti-money laundering law. Amendments in force since March 26, 2026 raised the maximum amounts up to 40 times and added compliance agreements and compliance orders.
- [MSB registration denied, revoked or expired: what happens and what to do](https://amlcanada.ca/msb-registration-refused-revoked.html): FINTRAC can deny an MSB application or revoke a registration for a short list of reasons set out in the Act. A registration that isn't renewed expires. Each outcome has its own deadlines, and operating without a valid registration is an offence.
- [Can you use a virtual office for FINTRAC MSB registration?](https://amlcanada.ca/virtual-office-msb-registration.html): FINTRAC's published guidance doesn't say whether a virtual office is acceptable. It does say what counts as a place of business in Canada, what the registration asks about your addresses, and that FINTRAC can check the information you give it.
- [RPAA safeguarding of end-user funds](https://amlcanada.ca/rpaa-safeguarding-end-user-funds.html): Since September 8, 2025, a payment service provider that holds funds for its users must safeguard them, either in trust in a trust account or in a segregated account backed by insurance or a guarantee. It also needs a written safeguarding framework and an independent review at least every three years.
- [FINTRAC compliance program requirements](https://amlcanada.ca/fintrac-compliance-program-requirements.html): Every business FINTRAC regulates must establish and implement a compliance program. It has five parts: a compliance officer, written policies and procedures, a risk assessment, an ongoing training program and plan, and a review of the program at least every two years.
- [The first 90 days of AML compliance after FINTRAC registration](https://amlcanada.ca/first-90-days-aml-compliance-canada.html): Once a money services business in Canada is registered with FINTRAC, its obligations apply from the day it starts operating. This guide sets out a practical order for the first three months and the legal deadlines to put in your diary.
- [FINTRAC MSB change of ownership: what to report and when](https://amlcanada.ca/fintrac-msb-change-of-ownership.html): When a registered money services business changes hands, its registration stays with the company, but FINTRAC has to be told about the changes within 30 days.
- [Ready-made FINTRAC MSB companies: what you get and what to question](https://amlcanada.ca/ready-made-msb-company-canada.html): A ready-made MSB is a Canadian company that's already registered with FINTRAC, sold through a share purchase. Here's what should come with one, and which sales claims don't hold up.
- [MSB licence in Canada: what FINTRAC registration really is](https://amlcanada.ca/msb-licence-canada.html): People search for a Canadian "MSB licence". What FINTRAC actually gives a money services business is a registration, and the difference matters when you buy, bank or advertise one.
- [Outsourced or in-house compliance officer?](https://amlcanada.ca/outsourced-vs-in-house-compliance-officer.html): Every business FINTRAC regulates needs a compliance officer. You can appoint the owner or a manager, hire someone, or outsource the role, and FINTRAC's expectations are the same in each case.
- [Buying an MSB in Canada: what to check](https://amlcanada.ca/buying-an-msb-canada.html): Buying a company that's already registered with FINTRAC as a money services business needs the same care as any acquisition, plus checks specific to FINTRAC and, for payment businesses, the Bank of Canada.
- [Preparing for a FINTRAC examination](https://amlcanada.ca/fintrac-examination-preparation.html): A FINTRAC examination usually starts with a call to your compliance officer and a letter asking for documents. Examinations can be done remotely or on site, and findings can lead to follow-up or a penalty.
- [The two-year effectiveness review: a checklist](https://amlcanada.ca/fintrac-effectiveness-review-checklist.html): FINTRAC requires every reporting entity to review its compliance program at least every two years. The review should test how the program works in practice as well as what's written down.
- [Registering a crypto business with FINTRAC](https://amlcanada.ca/crypto-registration-canada.html): Crypto exchanges and virtual currency dealers register with FINTRAC as money services businesses, whether they're based in Canada or serve Canadians from abroad.
- [What is the RPAA?](https://amlcanada.ca/rpaa-registration-guide.html): The Retail Payment Activities Act is the federal law under which the Bank of Canada supervises payment service providers. It sets rules on operational risk, incidents and the safeguarding of users' funds.
- [FINTRAC reporting for MSBs: which report, and when](https://amlcanada.ca/fintrac-reporting-requirements.html): Money services businesses report suspicious transactions, large cash, international transfers, large virtual currency receipts and listed person property to FINTRAC. Each report has its own trigger and deadline.
- [Foreign MSB registration in Canada](https://amlcanada.ca/foreign-msb-registration-canada.html): A business with no office in Canada may still have to register with FINTRAC. It does if it directs and provides money services to people or entities in Canada.
- [How much does MSB registration cost in Canada?](https://amlcanada.ca/msb-registration-cost-canada.html): FINTRAC doesn't charge a fee to register a money services business. The costs come from criminal record checks, translations, documents and the compliance program you need to operate.
- [How to register an MSB in Canada](https://amlcanada.ca/how-to-register-msb-canada.html): A money services business must register with FINTRAC before it starts operating, and renew every two years. FINTRAC doesn't charge a fee, and it says the majority of complete applications are processed within three months.
